source_text: Ἐν ἀμφοτέραις μὲν οὖν ταῖς ἐντολαῖς ἀγάπην εἰσηγεῖται, τάξει δ᾿ αὐτὴν διῄρηκε, καὶ ὅπου μὲν τὰ πρωτεῖα τῆς ἀγάπης ἀνάπτει τῷ θεῷ, ὅπου δὲ τὰ δευτερεῖα νέμει τῷ πλησίον. τίς δ᾿ ἂν ἄλλος οὗτος εἴη πλὴν αὐτὸς ὁ σωτήρ; ἢ τίς μᾶλλον ἡμᾶς ἐλεήσας ἐκείνου, τοῦς ὑπὸ τῶν κοσμοκρατόρων τοῦ σκότους ὀλίγου τεθανατωμένους τοῖς πολλοῖς τραύμασι. φόβοις, ἐπιθυμίαις. ὀργαῖς, λύπαις, ἀπάταις, ἡδοναῖς; τούτων δὲ τῶν τραυμάτων μόνος ἰατρὸς Ἰησοῦς, ἐκκόπτων ἄρδην τὰ πάθη πρόρριζα, οὐχ ὥσπερ ὁ νόμος ψιλὰ τὰ ἀποτελέσματα, τοὺς καρποὺς τῶν πονηρῶν φυτῶν, ἀλλὰ τὴν ἀξίνην τὴν ἑαυτοῦ πρὸς τὰς ῥίζας τῆς κακίας προσαγαγών. οὗτος ὁ τὸν οἶνον. τὸ αἷμα τῆς ἀμπέλου τῆς Δαβίδ, ἐκχέας ἡμῶν ἐπὶ τὰς τετρωμένας ψυχάς, οὗτος ὁ τὸ ἔλαιον, τὸν ἐκ σπλάγχνων πατρὸς ἔλεον, προσενεγκὼν καὶ ἐπιδαψιλευόμενος, οὗτος ὁ τοὺς τῆς ὑγείας καὶ σωτηρίας δεσμοὺς ἀλύτους ἐπιδείξας, ἀγάπην, πίστιν, ἐλπίδα, οὗτος ὁ διακονεῖν ἀγγέλους καὶ ἀρχὰς καὶ ἐξουσίας ἡμῖν ἐπιτάξας ἐπὶ μεγάλῳ μισθῷ, διότι καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐλευθερωθήσονται ἀπὸ τῆς ματαιότητος τοῦ κόσμου παρὰ τὴν ἀποκάλυψιν τῆς δόξης τῶν υἱῶν τοῦ θεοῦ. τοῦτον οὖν ἀγαπᾶν ἴσα χρὴ τῷ θεῷ. ἀγαπᾷ δὲ Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν ὁ τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ ποιῶν καὶ φυλάσσων αὐτοῦ τὰς ἐντολάς. »οὐ γὰρ πᾶς ὁ λέγων μοι ›κύριε κύριε‹ εἰσελεύσεται εἰς τὴν τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἀλλ᾿ ὁ ποιῶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός μου.« καί· »τί με λέγετε ›κύριε κύριε‹ καὶ οὐ ποιεῖτε ἃ λέγω;« καί· »ὑμεῖς μακάριοι οἱ ὁρῶντες καὶ ἀκούοντες ἃ μήτε δίκαιοι μήτε προφῆται«, ἐὰν ποιῆτε ἃ λέγω.
thought_title: Christ alone is the Samaritan who heals our wounds
orientation: Clement is explaining the parable of the Good Samaritan: the Samaritan is Christ, who alone heals the wounds inflicted by the passions, and loving him is equal to loving God.
pass_a_gloss: In both [the] commandments then he introduces love, but in order he has divided it, and where [on the one hand] he kindles the first [prizes] of love to God, where [on the other hand] he assigns the second [prizes] to [the] neighbor. Who then would this other be except [the] Savior himself? Or who [has] pitied us more than that one, [us] the [ones] by the world-rulers of the darkness almost put to death with many wounds—fears, desires, angers, griefs, deceits, pleasures? Of these wounds [the] only physician [is] Jesus, cutting out completely the passions root and branch, not as the law [cuts] bare the results, the fruits of the evil plants, but having brought his own axe to the roots of wickedness. This [is] the one [who] the wine, the blood of the vine of David, poured out on our wounded souls, this [is] the one [who] the oil, the mercy from [the] bowels of [the] Father, offered and lavished, this [is] the one [who] the bonds of health and salvation unbreakable showed, love, faith, hope, this [is] the one [who] to serve [us] angels and rulers and authorities commanded for us for great reward, because they also will be freed from the vanity of the world at the revelation of the glory of the sons of God. This one therefore to love equally [it is] necessary with God. And [he] loves Christ Jesus the [one] doing his will and keeping his commandments. "For not everyone saying to me 'Lord, Lord' will enter into the kingdom of heaven, but the [one] doing the will of my Father." And: "Why do you call me 'Lord, Lord' and do not do what I say?" And: "Blessed [are] you the [ones] seeing and hearing what neither righteous [ones] nor prophets," if you do what I say.

choices.why: πρωτεῖα means first prize or first place; 'first honors' keeps the competitive ranking imagery Clement uses for the two commandments
The compound κοσμοκράτωρ is a title for hostile spiritual powers; keeping 'world-rulers' preserves the cosmic scope and the genitive 'of the darkness' marks their domain

choices.english: cutting out the passions completely, root and branch
choices.why: ἄρδην means utterly or from the ground up, and πρόρριζα means by the roots; together they convey total eradication, which is Clement's point about Christ versus the law

choices.english: the mercy from the Father's bowels
choices.why: σπλάγχνα literally means inward parts or bowels, the seat of compassion in Greek idiom; keeping the bodily word preserves the vividness of the Father's mercy
rejected: the compassion from the Father's heart

choices.english: we must love equally with God
choices.why: ἴσα is adverbial 'equally'; the construction means Christ is to be loved to the same degree as God, which is Clement's bold claim here
rejected: it is necessary to love him as God
we must love him like God

bible_refs.note: οὐ γὰρ πᾶς ὁ λέγων μοι κύριε κύριε εἰσελεύσεται εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἀλλ᾽ ὁ ποιῶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός μου
τί με λέγετε κύριε κύριε καὶ οὐ ποιεῖτε ἃ λέγω

pass_b_english: In both commandments, then, he introduces love, but he has divided it by rank: in the one he kindles the first honors of love for God, and in the other he assigns the second honors to the neighbor. Who else could this be but the Savior himself? Or who has shown us more mercy than he—us, who were nearly put to death by the world-rulers of the darkness with many wounds: fears, desires, fits of anger, griefs, deceptions, pleasures? Of these wounds the only physician is Jesus, who cuts out the passions completely, root and branch. He does not do what the law does, which deals only with the bare results, the fruits of the wicked plants; instead he brings his own axe to the roots of evil. This is the one who poured out the wine—the blood of the vine of David—upon our wounded souls. This is the one who brought the oil—the mercy from the Father's bowels—and lavished it on us. This is the one who showed us the unbreakable bonds of health and salvation: love, faith, hope. This is the one who commanded angels and rulers and authorities to serve us for a great reward, because they too will be set free from the futility of the world at the revelation of the glory of the sons of God. Him, then, we must love equally with God. And the one who loves Christ Jesus is the one who does his will and keeps his commandments. "For not everyone who says to me, 'Lord, Lord,' will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of my Father" (Matthew 7:21). And: "Why do you call me 'Lord, Lord,' and do not do what I say?" (Luke 6:46). And: "Blessed are you who see and hear what neither the righteous nor the prophets saw or heard" (Luke 10:23–24)—if you do what I say.

problems.quote: Who else could this neighbor be but the Savior himself?
problems.source_quote: τίς δ᾿ ἂν ἄλλος οὗτος εἴη πλὴν αὐτὸς ὁ σωτήρ;
problems.why: The Greek says “Who else could this be but the Savior himself?”; English adds “neighbor,” altering the meaning.
problems.fix: Who else could this be but the Savior himself?

problems.source_quote: ὑμεῖς μακάριοι οἱ ὁρῶντες καὶ ἀκούοντες ἃ μήτε δίκαιοι μήτε προφῆται
problems.why: The wording 'what neither the righteous nor the prophets' matches Luke 10:23–24, not Matthew 13:16.
problems.ruling: Greek phrase corresponds to Matthew 13:17, not Matthew 13:16

edits.old: Who else could this neighbor be but the Savior himself?
edits.new: Who else could this be but the Savior himself?

fixed: Removed 'neighbor' from 'Who else could this neighbor be but the Savior himself?' because the Greek τίς δ᾿ ἂν ἄλλος οὗτος εἴη πλὴν αὐτὸς ὁ σωτήρ; refers to 'this' (οὗτος), not 'this neighbor'.
Changed scripture citation from Matthew 13:16 to Luke 10:23–24 because the wording 'what neither the righteous nor the prophets' matches Luke 10:23–24.

last_rejected.quote: the mercy from the Father's bowels—and lavished it on us.
last_rejected.why: Source says he 'brought' the oil and 'lavished it'; English 'brought … and lavished it on us' omits that the oil is applied to wounded souls.
last_rejected.fix: the mercy from the Father's bowels—and lavished it upon our wounded souls.
last_rejected.ruling: Greek says oil is brought and anointed (applied) to the wounded souls; English says brought and lavished on us – same sense, omission of “wounded souls” is minor.
